name: Hakusan
tagline: Otemachi in 10 minutes and Tokyo in 16 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000.
summary: The station is in Bunkyo City, served by Toei Mita Line. Journey times to the main business districts are 10 minutes to Otemachi, 25 minutes to Shinjuku, 28 minutes to Shibuya and 30 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. The station stands 13.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 16.7 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 13.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 8.1 m to 24.8 m, a difference of 16.7 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 1 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is less than 0.5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 12 clinics and 15 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 日本医科大学附属病院, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 都立駒込病院, about 17 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Toei Mita Line.
congestion: Toei Mita Line runs at 146% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 西巣鴨→巣鴨, which this station is not on. At 100%, the ministry's scale describes every passenger either seated or able to hold a strap or pillar. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥90,000 to ¥100,000 and 1K ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. 1LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000 and 2LDK ¥240,000 to ¥250,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is among the lowest in the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth and schools and parks within walking distance pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Hon-Komagome is ahead on quiet, but Hakusan is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hakusan. Hon-Komagome has the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line, a different set from Hakusan. To Otemachi, for instance, Hon-Komagome takes 8 minutes longer. On quiet, Hon-Komagome comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Todaimae is ahead on the number of medical facilities and quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Hakusan. Todaimae has the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line, a different set from Hakusan. To Otemachi, for instance, Todaimae takes 6 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥6,000 less at Todaimae. On quiet, Todaimae comes out ahead.

leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Toei Mita Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
